messages.subject: Three-level Model Implementation
parts:
I have the rate of occurrence of positive results of a given event, over time. I've been modelling this using the following Stan file:

data {
    int <lower = 1> number_rows;
    int <lower = 1> number_countries;
    vector [number_rows] day;
    int total [number_rows];
    int yes [number_rows];
    int <upper = number_countries> country [number_rows];
}

parameters {
    vector <lower = 0, upper = 1> [number_countries] initial;
    vector <lower = 0, upper = 1> [number_countries] asymptote;
    vector <lower = 0> [number_countries] scale;
    
    real<lower = 0> initial_alpha;
    real<lower = 0> initial_beta;
    real<lower = 0> asymptote_alpha;
    real<lower = 0> asymptote_beta;
    real<lower = 0> scale_alpha;
    real<lower = 0> scale_beta;
}

model {
    
    initial ~ beta(initial_alpha, initial_beta);
    asymptote ~ beta(asymptote_alpha, asymptote_beta);
    scale ~ inv_gamma(scale_alpha, scale_beta);
    
    yes ~ binomial (total, asymptote [country] + scale [country] .* (initial [country] - asymptote [country]) / (scale [country] + day));
}

where "yes" is the number of times the event came out positive on a given day for a given country and "total" is the number of times the event occurred on that day for that country. I expect the rate to follow the functional form as described (A + S * (I - S) / (S + day)), and I'm using a multilevel model where the population in question is the country. Ignoring for the moment the theoretical adequacy of the chosen priors, this performs marvelously, and I get very good results.

Now, I want to run an A/B test on this event, so I want to add a level between the level of the data and the level of the country: the level of the group. I wrote the following file for it:

data {
    int <lower = 1> number_rows;
    int <lower = 1> number_countries;
    int <lower = 1> number_ab_group;
    vector [number_rows] day;
    int total [number_rows];
    int yes [number_rows];
    int <upper = number_countries> country [number_rows];
    int <upper = number_ab_group> ab_group [number_rows];
}

parameters {
    matrix <lower = 0, upper = 1> [number_countries, number_ab_group] initial;
    matrix <lower = 0, upper = 1> [number_countries, number_ab_group] asymptote;
    matrix <lower = 0> [number_countries, number_ab_group] scale;
    
    vector <lower = 0> [number_countries] initial_alpha;
    vector <lower = 0> [number_countries] initial_beta;
    vector <lower = 0> [number_countries] asymptote_alpha;
    vector <lower = 0> [number_countries] asymptote_beta;
    vector <lower = 0> [number_countries] scale_alpha;
    vector <lower = 0> [number_countries] scale_beta;
    
    real <lower = 0> initial_alpha_alpha;
    real <lower = 0> initial_alpha_beta;
    real <lower = 0> initial_beta_alpha;
    real <lower = 0> initial_beta_beta;
    real <lower = 0> asymptote_alpha_alpha;
    real <lower = 0> asymptote_alpha_beta;
    real <lower = 0> asymptote_beta_alpha;
    real <lower = 0> asymptote_beta_beta;
    real <lower = 0> scale_alpha_alpha;
    real <lower = 0> scale_alpha_beta;
    real <lower = 0> scale_beta_alpha;
    real <lower = 0> scale_beta_beta;
}

model {
    initial_alpha ~ gamma(initial_alpha_alpha, initial_alpha_beta);
    initial_beta ~ gamma(initial_beta_alpha, initial_beta_beta);
    asymptote_alpha ~ gamma(asymptote_alpha_alpha, asymptote_alpha_beta);
    asymptote_beta ~ gamma(asymptote_beta_alpha, asymptote_beta_beta);
    scale_alpha ~ gamma(scale_alpha_alpha, scale_alpha_beta);
    scale_beta ~ gamma(scale_beta_alpha, scale_beta_beta);
    
    for(c in 1:number_countries){
        initial [c] ~ beta(initial_alpha [c], initial_beta [c]);
        asymptote [c] ~ beta(asymptote_alpha [c], asymptote_beta [c]);
        scale [c] ~ inv_gamma(scale_alpha [c], scale_beta [c]);
    }
    
    for (i in 1: number_rows) yes [i] ~ binomial (total [i], asymptote [country [i], ab_group [i]] + scale [country [i], ab_group [i]] * (initial [country [i], ab_group [i]] - asymptote [country [i], ab_group [i]]) / (scale [country [i], ab_group [i]] + dsi [i]));
}

Is it correct? Is there a better way to do it? I tried it and it gives me terrible fit, but I'm not sure how to improve.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Three-level Model Implementation
parts:
I'm not sure what you mean by work. You've added another level
to the model. But you've forced the two groups to share priors,
with
matrix <lower = 0> [number_countries, number_ab_group] scale;

...
for(c in 1:number_countries){
...

scale [c] ~ inv_gamma(scale_alpha [c], scale_beta [c]);
}

I'm not sure if that's what you want. It won't give you the same
result as running the two (?) groups separately. For that, you'd
need to do this the other way around.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Three-level Model Implementation
parts:
Sorry --- didn't answer this before.

But no, there's not an equivalent to the vectorization for
matrices. The speed is probably not from the loops. The
vectorization is just for convenience and unfolds to the
same kind of looping code. The savings come from passing
vectorized argument to the lpdf and lpmf functions.

- Bob
